clue.text: Truck even has somewhere to sleep

a bed is a place to sleep

explanation.surface: A lorry driver's cab comes with a bunk for overnight stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatbed is a lorry with an open, sideless platform for carrying loads, so it is a kind of truck.

clue.text: Return of live Sky broadcast is quaintly traditional

the broadcaster's name, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rerun of a live Sky programme feels charmingly old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite TV company; 'Return' seems to apply to the live show but only turns the word 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Folksy describes something homely and rustic in style, which is what quaintly traditional means.

clue.text: Frank possibly has Capone's temper

parts.note: Anne Frank, the diarist, is one person with the surname Frank
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: Someone's friend shares the gangster's notorious short fuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a first name or an adjective for honest; it is a surname, and 'possibly' says the answer is one example of a Frank.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper metal or glass is to toughen it by heating and slow cooling, which is exactly what annealing does.

clue.text: Warm yourself before ballet movement, sport!

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to a dancer: warm up before rehearsing a ballet movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Basketball is a team game, so it is an example of a sport.

clue.text: Call at first-rate city

parts.note: to dub someone is to call or name them
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as letter I

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop off at a top-class city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is the largest city of the United Arab Emirates, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Sinks on the wagon left covered with spots

TT, teetotal, describes someone off alcohol
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A sober drinker collapses, abandoned and covered in a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a noun for pimples but is the verb meaning notices.
explanation.definitionFit: When sediment sinks to the bottom it settles; both verbs mean to drop down and come to rest.

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
letters to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Synthetic means artificially made rather than natural, so manufactured is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sleeper separators consisting of wrought iron caps in hollow train bases

caps sit on top, so only the leading letters of the two metal words are kept

a bed is a base, as a railway track bed or a flower bed

explanation.surface: Railway talk: what separates the sleepers under a track, made of iron and sitting in ballast beds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all railway sleepers; in the answer the sleepers are people, kept apart by having a bed each.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of single beds keeps the two people sleeping in a room apart, so twin beds playfully separate sleepers.

clue.text: Womanizer has short length, wavy hair, too

explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, from a seducer in an 18th-century play, is a byword for a man who chases women.

clue.text: Gents: HRT is fantastic for potency!

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful and unreal, so the letters are freely reimagined in another order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
letters to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Potency is power or force, so strength is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Associations making line printing essentials

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
a printer cannot print without inks

explanation.surface: Trade bodies set up so that printers can share the basics.
explanation.definitionFit: Links between people or things are connections, so they are associations.

clue.text: Record-breaking athlete is a handy help on a flight, you say?

indicators.note: you say points to the spoken form, so the word is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.words: a handy help on a flight
parts.note: a banister is the rail you hold going up a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: A sporting champion described as a useful hand on the stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel but means a flight of stairs; 'handy' because you grip it by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Bannister set a world record in 1954 by running the first mile in under four minutes.

clue.text: Audience's left with unusually great sight

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
letters to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as departed; it is the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage directions are given from the actor's view facing the house, so the actor's right side is the left as seen by the audience.

clue.text: State News author

read as new plus new, with each new abbreviated to N

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Mann was a German novelist, author of The Magic Mountain and Death in Venice.

clue.text: Company making top favourite cocktail ingredient alternative for rival

explanation.definitionFit: A competitor is someone you contend against, so a rival is a synonym.

clue.text: Initial boost galvanized reformer

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
letters to be rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'with no nuts' reads as a nut-free recipe; 'no' is fodder and 'nuts' the signal.

clue.text: Funny man needs a hand creating tropical island feature

parts.note: Coco the Clown was a famous circus clown
the palm is part of the hand

explanation.surface: A comedian wants applause for building a desert-island set.
explanation.definitionFit: Coconut palms fringe tropical beaches, the stock image of a desert island.

clue.text: Plant making American tin in that way

clue.text: Outsize builder's ledge round room for electronic instrument

room to manoeuvre is scope

explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a placement instruction but just supplies a letter shaped like a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: An oscilloscope displays electrical signals as traces on a screen, a standard electronic test instrument.

clue.text: Not for those who would mighty oaks from acorns grow?

definitions.text: Not for those who would mighty oaks from acorns grow?

parts.words: Not for those who would mighty oaks from acorns grow?
parts.note: surface reading: something that does not suit gardeners hoping for huge trees from small seeds
setter's reading: an art that deliberately keeps trees tiny, the opposite of the proverb

explanation.walkthrough: It plays on the proverb 'great oaks from little acorns grow'; this Japanese art does the reverse, keeping trees miniature.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the cultivation of dwarfed trees in pots, so no oak grown that way will become mighty.

clue.text: Arrival one day before opening

a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: Someone turns up a day before a grand opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means the coming or arrival of something, from Latin for coming to.

clue.text: 'Heroin kept inside' heard from pen inmate?

parts.note: found across the two words

explanation.walkthrough: The pen is a pigsty, not a prison, and its inmate a pig; 'heard' belongs to the definition, not a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the grunting noise a pig makes, the sound you would hear from a pigpen.

clue.text: It entitles board member to meet with mobster

a hood, or hoodlum, is a gangster

explanation.walkthrough: 'board member' suggests a company director; it is a chess piece.

clue.text: After a good time, extremely sweaty and flatulent

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.definitionFit: Flatulent means having wind in the gut, which is what gassy means of a person.

clue.text: Reportedly, one's smacked as a House supporter

explanation.walkthrough: 'smacked' looks like hit, but a smacker is slang for a loud kiss; House is the royal House of York, not Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yorkist backed the House of York against Lancaster in the Wars of the Roses.
